text: Our actions Research grants Research grants Each year, the Fyssen Foundation awards between four and six research grants to researchers leading innovative scientific projects. Research grants Objectives Fyssen Foundation research grants aim to facilitate the execution of research projects that enhance understanding of the mechanisms of behaviour and cognition in living beings, as well as their ontogenetic and phylogenetic development. These projects may originate from the disciplines of neuroscience, ethology, psychology, anthropology, ethnology, palaeontology, and archaeology. The specific goals of the grants include: Enabling young researchers to establish and lead a research group within an academic institution in France. Developing autonomous and innovative research themes. Promoting mobility and attracting high-level early career group leaders to foster a dynamic and progressive research environment. Eligibility criteria The Fyssen research grant is intended for young researchers of any nationality who have completed their doctoral thesis more than 3 years and less than 10 years ago (exceptions may be granted for maternity/paternity/long-term illness leave) *. Already employed, they will form a research team around them to carry out a collective scientific project within a host structure in France whose activity aligns with the objectives of the Foundation. Researchers may develop their project in a laboratory different from the one where they obtained their thesis or from the one where they currently work. Recipients of ATIP-Avenir or ANR Young Researchers funding are eligible for the Fyssen grant. ** The most innovative projects will be selected, based on the Foundation’s annual budget, at a rate of 3 to 5 projects per year. * The 10 years are counted from the date on which the doctorate is awarded to the date on which funding begins. For maternity leave, the actual time elapsed since the doctorate was awarded will be reduced by one year for each child. For paternity leave(s), the elapsed time will be reduced by the leave taken for each child born. For long-term sick leave, the elapsed time will be reduced by the duration of the period of absence. ** Recipients of support for young researchers such as ERC starting grant to develop an independent project are not eligible. Candidates who have applied for one of these types of funding and do not have the results at the time of submitting their Fyssen application are required to indicate this in their application and to inform the Fyssen Foundation as soon as possible in the event of a positive result from the ANR or ERC (in this case, Fyssen funding will be interrupted at the start date of the other funding). Grant Amount The research grant amount is up to €100,000. The research grant is intended to cover the following expenses: Purchase of equipment and small materials useful for research work; Consumables required for conducting research work; Salaries (except for the principal investigator); Specialized services necessary for the research work; Travel expenses: for conducting the research project or for attending scientific conferences and symposiums; Publication costs. The management fees of the supervising organization will not be covered by the Fyssen Foundation research grant. Duration of the Grant The Fyssen research grant is awarded for a period of one year (12 months) and is non-renewable. Article Submission at the end of the grant : The funding agreement for the grant must include the following statement: “The recipient commits to submitting an article to the Editorial Committee for possible publication in the Annals of the Foundation.” The two best articles submitted to the Editorial Committee will be awarded a prize of €1,000 each. * The 10 years are counted from the date on which the doctorate is awarded to the date on which funding begins. The application folder should include the following documents in PDF : The Research Grant application form An invitation letter from the host laboratory specifying the material conditions under which the researcher can carry out their research project The letters of two scientific personalities able to make an appreciation on the program and the research works of the candidate and who do not belong to the Host laboratory The applicant’s CV and the publications list The description of the research project (5, 8 pages maximum) The detailed description of the budget forecasts The list of the other financial supports The list of the people who will join the research team for the project The abstract (150 words) of the research project as well as a keywords list in French AND in English The copy of the authorization request sent to the Ethic Committee* if necessary The copy of the contract of employment Opening session on the web site: September, 1, 2026 The Fyssen foundation attaches great importance to the scientific integrity of the research it funds. It is essential that scientific research is conducted in accordance with general guiding principles of scientific integrity — honesty, diligence, transparency, reproducibility, independence, responsibility — as well in accordance with any more specific guiding principles used by the institutions and stakeholders with whom the applicant collaborates. When designing your research project, have you applied the code of conduct and ethic regulations of your institution as well as the ones of institutions and stakeholders with whom you will work? Download the poster Modus Operandi 1 Register – Click on “Apply”, then on “Registration” and complete the form. Your login credentials will be sent to you by email. 2 Complete your application – Log in to your personal account, provide the requested information and upload the required documents. This can be done in several sessions. 3 Submit your application – Once your application is complete, submit it definitively. 4 Submission confirmation – You will automatically receive an email confirming receipt of your application. 5 Application review – Your application is submitted to the Scientific Council. 6 Results – The results are communicated by email in December. FAQ How does the applicant get its login ? The applicant has to create its own login. Are there any exemptions for maternity/paternity leave? For maternity leave, one year per child will be deducted from the effective time elapsed since the PhD defense. For paternity leave, the effective time elapsed since the PhD defense will be reduced by the actual duration of the leave taken for each child born. What are the earliest and latest possible project start dates? The project must start between January and May, inclusive. May the project be drafted in english ? Yes, the project proposal must be written in English. Can I apply if I am on a fixed-term contract? Yes, provided that your contract covers the entire period during which you will use the grant. In what language should the required letters be written? In French or English. The candidate has submitted documents with errors. Can they update them? Yes, they can update a document as long as they have not yet definitively submitted their application online. Once the application has been locked, the candidate may still contact the Foundation and provide a new document.
